steps.body: The grid reads any hundredths decimal: full columns show the tenths digit, single cells show the hundredths digit.
steps.narration: The grid reads any hundredths decimal: full columns show the tenths digit, single cells show the hundredths digit.

widget.prompt: Shade the grid to show 0.37. Each full column is one tenth; each cell is one hundredth.

commonCounts.feedback: That shades only 7 single cells. The tenths digit of 0.37 is worth whole columns: 3 full columns first, then 7 more cells.
That count swaps the digits of 0.37. The first digit after the point counts full columns; the second counts single cells.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly 37 of the 100 cells — 3 full columns and 7 more cells: 37 hundredths, written 0.37.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Fill whole columns for the tenths digit first, then single cells for the hundredths.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each full column is one tenth — check the tenths digit before adding single cells.

predict.prompt: To shade 0.37, how many of the 100 cells will you fill in all?
predict.reveal: The 3 in the tenths place is worth 3 full columns — 30 cells — and the 7 adds seven more: 37 cells.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g4d hundredths grid.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g4d hundredths grid must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g4d hundredths grid.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 0.52 needs 5 full columns plus 2 cells: 52 in all.
0.52 is 52 hundredths, so 52 cells must be shaded.

widget.prompt: A hundredths grid has 100 equal cells. How many cells must be shaded to show 0.52?

commonErrors.feedback: That shades only the tenths digit's worth of single cells. In 0.52 the 5 sits in the tenths place, so it is worth 5 full columns — 50 cells — before the hundredths digit adds any more.
That count swaps the two digits of 0.52. Read the decimal place by place: the first digit after the point counts full columns of ten, and the second counts single cells.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Each full column of the grid is one tenth — ten cells — and each single cell is one hundredth. Turn each digit of the decimal into cells and add the two counts.

widget.prompt: A unit square is split into 100 equal cells, and 28 of them are shaded. Write the shaded amount as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the count of shaded cells, and a count of parts is a whole number. Each cell is one hundredth of the square, so the count belongs after the decimal point, ending in the hundredths place.
That reads the count as tenths, but each cell is one hundredth of the square — a tenth is a whole column of 10 cells. Write the count so it ends in the hundredths place.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Each cell is one hundredth. Write the count of shaded cells so its last digit lands in the hundredths place — two places after the decimal point.
